maria: quick PSA 3 bringing up Aurelia-13B (Gemma fork) on int4 and hit two oddities: 1) combining diacritics are being emitted as separate tokens (e.g. "é" -> [ 'e', '́' ]), 2) rotary frequency per-head seems inconsistent after quantization (some heads show ~0.6x expected frequency). reproducible on a tiny prompt.
kevin: can you paste the exact convert command + the tokenizer config and which quant backend?
maria: command: `python tools/convert.py --src=models/gemma/aurelia.ckpt --out=ggml/aurelia-int4.bin --quant=int4-gemmlowp --fold-headwise-rotary`. Tokenizer excerpt from model repo: `{"normalize": false, "split_on_whitespace": false, "version": 1}`. sample tokens for "Café": `[101, 2048, 13723, 3]` (expected one token for "é").
anand: that token split screams lack of NFC/NFKC normalization. upstream tokenizers often assume normalized input. is this tokenizer the model-provided one?
maria: yes, it's the repo's tokenizer. I didn't run our normal lexnorm step. tiny dump: `token_map[13723] = '́' # COMBINING ACUTE`.
julie: for rotary: how did you measure the per-head frequency? simple FFT/angle slope probe?
maria: quick probe: take the rotary cos/sin table per head and compute phase slope across positions. snippet: ```python
# probe rotary slope per head
for h in range(n_heads):
    tab = rotary_table[h][:200]
    phases = np.arctan2(tab[:,1], tab[:,0])
    slope = np.polyfit(np.arange(len(phases)), phases, 1)[0]
    print(h, slope)
```
kevin: if convert.py folded a per-head scale into the table to compress ranges, a bug in the fold could alter effective frequency. did the converter have a headwise-scale pass?
maria: yes `--fold-headwise-rotary` enabled that pass. i ran a float->int4 run without the flag as a quick sanity, and the slope variance disappeared. the int4 with fold showed several heads at ~0.6x slope.
anand: sounds like two independent issues: tokenizer normalization + headwise rotary folding bug. plan: 1) try pre-tokenizer NFC normalization and see tokens collapse, 2) rerun conversion with `--rotary-uniform` (disable folding) to confirm, 3) run a small eval (10 docs) comparing int4-folded, int4-uniform, and fp32 baseline for rouge/qa-em.
maria: ran NFC pre-normalize -> "Café" tokens now `[101, 2048, 13723_combined, 3]` (single token). reran convert with `--rotary-uniform` -> per-head slopes align with fp32. quick run of `echo "The quick brown fox" | python run.py --model ggml/aurelia-int4.bin --tokens 64` shows longctx cosine sim to fp32 baseline improved from 0.72 -> 0.95. rouge delta: folded-int4 vs fp32 = -0.8, uniform-int4 vs fp32 = -0.05 (10-sample).
julie: great. suggests tokenizer NFC fix mandatory; rotary folding should be opt-in and guarded. for shipping we want tokenizer change in model repo (or runtime lexnorm) and converter patch to require explicit opt-in with regression tests.
kevin: agree. i'll add a converter unit test that simulates a headwise scale and checks effective frequency preserved within tolerance after quant fold. also add a flag `--allow-headwise-fold` default false.
anand: i'll own the review. julie, can you run the larger eval (200 examples) across summarization and qa? include tokenization metric (fraction of combining marks split) and longctx sim.
julie: will run overnight and post results tomorrow morning.
ci-bot: ci/onboard-aurelia triggered: 2 flaky tests (tokenization/regression). logs: https://ci.redwood/runs/23456
maria: opening PRs now: 1) enable NFC pre-tokenize in our ingestion pipeline + unit test, 2) converter change to opt-in headwise fold and unit tests. linking shortly. :white_check_mark:
kevin: nice find. lesson: always run lexnorm + double-check any per-head transform in quant pipeline.
maria: thanks all — saved us a nasty long-context drift. will follow up with PR links.
ci-bot: PRs opened: #276-tokenizer-nfc-ensure, #277-rotary-fold-optin. CI: running full eval (ETA ~40m).
